title: Farm project
titleCn: 农场项目：设计一个假想农场

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Hi, Dave. Ready to start on our farm project about creating a hypothetical farm?
Yes. It's gonna take much work to create a hypothetical farm, so I don't wanna procrastinate.
We have lots of time. It's not due for a while. But you're right, it's going to be quite a challenge, and I want to make sure no one else takes our choice of topic.
No, the professor said any group can pick any choices, so that doesn't matter. But I really need a good grade on this.
Me too. So it's good we're starting early. Let's go through the project outline and map out everything. First, we need to choose the type of farm we want to create, right?
Yes. So we've got a lot of decisions to make. What kind of farm operation it'll be and where it'll be located, how big it needs to be. Uh, that could be a problem. [chuckles] I'm not good at math.
Hmm. It's not an easy decision to make. What else? We'd have to think about how the farm would be organized and who has responsibility for what.
That work we did on management systems should be useful there. Then, of course, we've got to decide what would actually be grown on our farm. Hmm, that won't be easy.
No, we've got to get that right. Once we do, we can go ahead and think about things like how the whole farm would be laid out.
Yeah. I'm looking forward to that bit.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.
Well, let's discuss our crop options.
Hmm. Maybe a vine crop like grapes.
Or a tree farm, maybe apples or peaches.
Or strawberries.
Strawberries? Apples would be easier.
Well, I know you've got to be a bit careful with strawberries to get the right type of soil for them to grow in and to prevent diseases, but they always taste great. Well, I think so anyway.
We'd be selling them, not eating them, though.
Oh, sure. But they give us so many options.
Okay, let's go with strawberries. Let's move on.
Uh, it says here to decide early if we're going to do organic or conventional fruit production.

I'd like to do organic. I don't think growing organic is more difficult, just different, and I think our consumers would go for it. But we'll have to look at the numbers to see if it's economically feasible, and if there really is a health advantage.
Okay. Site selection is another decision for us.
Should we choose a traditional farm way out in the country?
Hmm. It's tempting, but it'll be easier to pick a geographic location we're more familiar with.
Okay. Then let's just choose somewhere near here. Plus, then it will be easier to look at the newspaper to get an idea of the prices of farms.
That's good. Uh, I'm nervous about this step.
Buying the farm? Well, it does need a lot of research.

Ah, yes, I know. I just don't know where to start. I suppose I'll feel better about it once I've done that. Anyway, at least it's all hypothetical. We're not really having to pay out our own money for it, and actually, there probably won't be too many to choose from.
Agreed. Now, we need to choose a proper, um... What's that called when a particular variety of crop is bred to exhibit certain characteristics? A cultivar, that's it.

Hmm. I'm confident about this step. If we choose a good location, we should be able to pick a couple of good varieties with desirable characteristics to do well. In fact, in last week's reading, it talked about the three best strawberry varieties in our region.
Right. We'll only need one good cultivar since strawberries can be harvested from the same plants for two or more months, which is the entire growing season.
You're right. Imagine if we were doing peaches or plums. More variety, shorter harvesting periods, much more complicated. Hmm. We've made a good choice.
We have to figure the number of acres we're going to cultivate, though.
Yes, and the machinery we'll need, the prices we'll charge for picking.

And how we'll attract customers, the whole advertising campaign. And don't forget, we also have to create a map to scale of our site, showing everything from the direction of our rows, equipment storage, office, parking lot, irrigation systems, just as if it were a real farm. That's the bit I'll enjoy most, I think.
Yes. And I see finally here it says we need to do a complete economic analysis. Ah, you'll be good at that.
I hope our imaginary farm is profitable.
Me too.

You know, when I first signed up for this class, I thought I wanted to study agriculture or plant science, but finding out about the business side of farming has been a real bonus. Although the math still scares me.
It's a good thing you have me for a partner then. We make a good team.
Definitely. Well, I'll see you in class tomorrow.
Bye.
